title: Near-blowup asymptotic analysis and analytical extension for the inviscid primitive equations
summary: The primitive equations widely approximate the Navier--Stokes equations in large-scale geophysical fluid dynamics. Their finite-time singularity formation-which occurs exclusively in the inviscid case-sheds light on the mechanisms driving small-scale creation. Building on \cite{Collot2023}, which constructed 2D horizontally odd solutions where the on-axis derivative $\partial_X u(t,0,Z)$ blows up at rate $(T-t)^{-1}$ with boundary concentration scale $|\ln (T-t)|^{-1}$, this paper characterizes this blow-up as forming between hyperbolic stagnation points.
